A national university in Busan, one of Korea's largest public universities, with international admission that accepts either Korean or English proficiency evidence and score-based scholarships.
PNU publishes tuition in its admission materials; as a national university its fees are lower than most private universities, but the figures were not read during this check
Department of Global Studies — English, Busan campus
Published scope: Spring 2027 only; Fall rules not established

Ordinary category: IELTS 5.5, TOEFL iBT 80 (guide new scale 4) or New TEPS 327. TOPIK is not compulsory for Global Studies. Nationality-specific higher thresholds prevent one universal numerical minimum.
The guide lists US, UK, Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand and South Africa; confirm the required school-history evidence with admissions.

Nepalese, Mongolian, Vietnamese and Uzbek applicants: IELTS 7 or TOEFL iBT 85 (guide new scale 5) for Global Studies, and TOPIK 5 for Korean routes. The ordinary departmental minimum must not be applied to these categories.
Pusan Spring 2027 undergraduate guide: English section
AI Computer Science and Engineering — Korean, Busan campus
Normally level 4 or PNU language level 4. With the specified English evidence, level 3/PNU level 3 may qualify; these majors are explicitly NOT English tracks.
— Depends on grades; a separate award pays ₩500,000 a month
One PNU scholarship pays ₩500,000 a month and can be held alongside grade-based awards; the tuition share was not read during this check.
Engineering, Business, Humanities, Social Sciences, Biology, Health & Medicine, Economics
Teaching is mainly in Korean; applicants can submit either Korean (TOPIK) or English proficiency evidence, and should check with the department whether their degree can be taken in English.

₩3,316,500 per semester for engineering (₩2,795,500 for business), fully waived for new international students
the published semester tuition before the waiver; accommodation, food and insurance are handled by the separate living scholarships
UNIST Fall 2027 international bachelor admission, Ulsan
Teaching language: Teaching language not confirmed · Direct admission

The complete 2027 guide requires TOEFL, IELTS, TEPS or TOEIC evidence, valid within two years of the application deadline, but does not publish numerical thresholds. A missing published number is not a confirmed zero minimum.
Applicants from the US, Canada, UK, Australia, New Zealand and Ireland are exempt in this guide. A general school-MOI exemption is not stated.
SAT/ACT/IB/A-level are in the supplementary document list, separately from required language evidence. TOPIK is supplementary too.
Application/study plan, school diploma and recent transcripts, identity/family evidence; authenticated originals after registration. Scholarship and non-scholarship admission tracks are distinct.
UNIST Fall 2027 full international undergraduate guide
— Full tuition in semester one; conditional renewal from semester two
— ₩75,000 a month, reimbursed on proof of payment

All international freshmen receive a full tuition waiver in their first semester. For their second semester, the published freshman exception requires 12 credits and GPA 2.0 for full tuition support. After that, 12 credits and GPA 2.7 qualify for a full waiver, while GPA 2.0 qualifies for half. Living-scholarship tiers are assigned on admission and have their own renewal criteria. Meals mean two per day during the semester. Health-insurance payments of KRW 75,000/month are reimbursed against proof. Housing and personal costs remain separate.
Engineering, Computer Science, Biology, Mathematics, Business
UNIST teaches its undergraduate courses in English; students choose a major track after a common first year.
